label: Every capped turn sits in the 300 s group: opencode 26, devin 20 (19 counted plus the restore-failed fresh-skill-04 null), pi 2, claude 0, dsh 0; no 900 s g2 row was ever cut.
The cap is keyed to row-set membership, not to observed behaviour: capForRow returns 900 s only for G2_PROMPTS, while fresh rows that launch /create:goal or /create:command are held to 300 s.
Twenty sampled turn durations run 15-298 s with four completions within 10 s of the 300 s cap on opencode, devin and dsh, so the cap slices a live tail rather than a hang.
A capped OpenCode session produced messages through 293 s of its 300 s and exited 143, while an uncapped sibling ran 291 s and exited 0.
A runtime-keyed cap is the wrong lever: claude and dsh capped 0 of 80 fresh runs each, so only a behaviour-keyed cap (900 s once a workflow opens) addresses the misclassified rows.
Hook cost is not a measurable share of a turn: p95 290 ms is 1.9 percent of the shortest sampled turn (15 s) and 0.10 percent of a 298 s turn; the 2,218 ms worst row is 0.7 percent of a 300 s turn.
The cap's cost is lost judgeable rows: 26 of 80 opencode fresh runs (32.5 percent) and 20 of 81 devin fresh runs (24.7 percent) ended capped, against 0 of 80 on claude and dsh.

reason: It leaves the row-set key in place and gives zero help to claude and dsh, which never capped.
